goal:
Create src/components/Body3DModel/urticariaSprite.ts so the EXISTING hand-written test src/components/Body3DModel/urticariaSprite.test.ts passes. Do NOT modify the test file — it is the specification.

The module draws ONE urticaria wheal (anaphylaxis rash) onto a 2D canvas context. Clinically a wheal is a raised, erythematous (red) ring with a paler blanched centre, irregular edges.

EXPORT: export function drawWheal(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, cx: number, cy: number, r: number, seed: number): void

RULES:
1. DETERMINISTIC: derive ALL randomness from `seed` via a small local PRNG (e.g. mulberry32). NEVER call Math.random — BodyMesh must get the identical rash every reload.
2. Wrap the whole drawing in ctx.save() ... ctx.restore() (balanced). If you use additional save/restore pairs internally, balance each one.
3. Draw a raised red wheal: an outer erythematous ring (reddish, e.g. rgba around (210, 70, 60)) via a radial gradient fill or a stroked ring, plus a paler/blanched centre (lighter, e.g. rgba around (235, 180, 170)). Use at least 4 real drawing ops total from {fill, stroke, arc, ellipse, lineTo, fillRect}. An irregular edge (a few arc/ellipse lobes offset by the PRNG) reads more like a real wheal than a perfect circle.
4. BOUNDS: every arc(x,y,...) and ellipse(x,y,...) centre must stay within 2.2*r of (cx, cy). Keep lobe offsets small (e.g. up to ~0.5*r).
5. Set fillStyle/strokeStyle/globalAlpha as needed (the test's ctx accepts any property set). Leave ctx state balanced.

Style: one pure function + a small PRNG helper, no imports, no classes, no console. Brief JSDoc.
verify: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json && npx vitest run src/components/Body3DModel/urticariaSprite.test.ts
